description: Ten waves, each after the last is cleared. Does mastery survive duration?
notes: A ten-wave siege, in the Killing Floor shape: discrete waves, each cleared before the next begins, escalating in composition rather than in enemy statistics.
**The hypothesis it tests** — and it is a different one from every other encounter here:

> Does mastery survive *duration*? Everything else in this file is 30-90 seconds, which > is long enough to observe an exchange but not long enough to observe fatigue, stamina > economy across a whole fight, or whether a player's timing degrades as they tire.
Two properties are load-bearing and deliberate:

**Every wave waits for a clear room** (`atMs: null`). That is what makes it a *progression* rather than a density curve — the player meets each composition at full health of attention, so a failure at wave 8 is about wave 8 and not about accumulated chaos. It is the opposite choice from `overlap_court`, on purpose, so the two can be compared.

**Difficulty escalates by composition only.** No wave buffs anyone's hp, damage or speed. The canon is emphatic that simple enemies with offset timings should produce richer mastery than statistically inflated ones (H11); scaling numbers here would quietly test the opposite claim and look like the same experiment.
The rhythm is 3 beats: guards teach the metronome (1-3), duelists break the rhythm (4-6), archers add the spacing axis (7-9), and 10 asks for all three at once.
Spawn points around the arena edge, so waves arrive from a readable direction.
1-3 — the metronome. Learn the guard's beat with nothing else in the room.
4-6 — the mix-up. A rhythm learned above will actively mislead here.
7-9 — the spacing axis. Melee pressure plus a threat that refuses melee.
10 — all three verbs at once. Deliberately not "more of wave 9": the test is whether
the player can switch between reads, not whether they can survive a bigger number.
Untimed. A clock would turn a fatigue study into a speed study, and the question here is
explicitly about what happens over a long fight.
